definition: Taking over a user's active login session by stealing the session token.
exampleSentence: Session hijacking lets an attacker act as you without knowing your password.

definition: Sending fake DNS answers to redirect users to a malicious website.
exampleSentence: Because of DNS spoofing, the bank's address opened a fake page.

definition: Sending fake ARP messages to redirect traffic inside a local network.
exampleSentence: ARP spoofing allowed the attacker to read traffic between two office computers.

definition: Faking the source IP address of packets to hide identity or trick a system.
exampleSentence: IP spoofing makes it hard to know where the attack traffic really comes from.

definition: Capturing and reading data that travels through a network.
exampleSentence: Packet sniffing on an unencrypted network can reveal login details in plain text.

definition: Checking which ports on a machine are open to find possible entry points.
exampleSentence: The logs showed port scanning from one address against all of our servers.

definition: Recording a valid message and sending it again to trick a system.
exampleSentence: A replay attack allowed the thief to open the car using a copied signal.

definition: A denial-of-service attack that sends many half-open connection requests.
exampleSentence: A SYN flood filled the connection table and the web server stopped answering.

definition: Putting false data into a DNS cache so that users are sent to wrong addresses.
exampleSentence: After DNS poisoning, many customers landed on a page controlled by criminals.

definition: A fake Wi-Fi hotspot that copies a real one to steal user data.
exampleSentence: At the airport, an evil twin network copied the name of the official hotspot.

definition: An unauthorized Wi-Fi device connected to a company network.
exampleSentence: Security found a rogue access point hidden under a desk in the meeting room.

definition: Forcing devices off a Wi-Fi network by sending fake disconnect messages.
exampleSentence: A deauthentication attack kept disconnecting our laptops from the office Wi-Fi.

definition: A bug where a program writes more data than a memory area can hold.
exampleSentence: A buffer overflow in the old software allowed attackers to run their own code.

definition: A flaw that lets an attacker run commands on a system from far away.
exampleSentence: The patch fixes a remote code execution bug that was already used in attacks.

definition: Inserting operating system commands into an app that does not check its input.
exampleSentence: Command injection happened because the script passed user text directly to the shell.

definition: Using special paths like ../ to read files outside the allowed folder.
exampleSentence: The path traversal bug exposed the server's configuration file to everyone.

definition: Tricking users into clicking a hidden button placed under a harmless-looking page.
exampleSentence: Clickjacking hides a real payment button behind a fake game on the screen.

definition: A flaw that lets attackers send users from a trusted site to a malicious one.
exampleSentence: Phishers abused an open redirect on our website to make their links look safe.

definition: An attack that makes a server send requests to places chosen by the attacker.
exampleSentence: The SSRF flaw let the attacker reach the internal cloud metadata service.

definition: An attack that abuses XML parsers to read files or call internal services.
exampleSentence: Disabling external entities in the parser prevents an XXE attack.

definition: A flaw where untrusted data is turned into objects and can run harmful code.
exampleSentence: Insecure deserialization allowed the attacker to upload a crafted object and take control.

definition: A flaw where changing an ID in a request shows another user's data.
exampleSentence: With an IDOR bug, changing the number in the URL showed someone else's invoice.

definition: Tricking a build system into downloading a malicious public package instead of a private one.
exampleSentence: Dependency confusion put a fake package with the same name into our build.

definition: An attack that works without any action from the victim.
exampleSentence: A zero-click exploit infected the phone as soon as the message arrived.

definition: A bug that lets code break out of an isolated environment.
exampleSentence: Researchers demonstrated a sandbox escape that gave them control of the whole browser.

definition: A flaw that lets code leave a container and reach the host machine.
exampleSentence: A container escape would give the attacker access to every other service on the node.

definition: Claiming an unused subdomain that still points to an external service.
exampleSentence: A forgotten DNS record led to a subdomain takeover on our marketing site.

definition: Using an API in ways its owner did not intend, often at large scale.
exampleSentence: Rate limits were added after API abuse slowed down the mobile application.

definition: Placing harmful content in a cache so that other users receive it.
exampleSentence: Cache poisoning made the CDN serve a malicious script to thousands of visitors.

definition: Sending specially crafted requests that confuse servers about where one request ends.
exampleSentence: HTTP request smuggling can bypass the security checks in front of the application.

definition: Stealing usernames, passwords or tokens to access accounts.
exampleSentence: After the credential theft, the attacker logged in like a normal employee.

definition: Using a stolen password hash to log in without knowing the real password.
exampleSentence: The pass-the-hash technique helped the intruder move between Windows servers quietly.

definition: Requesting service tickets in Windows networks to crack service account passwords offline.
exampleSentence: Kerberoasting works when service accounts have weak and old passwords.

definition: A forged Kerberos ticket that gives an attacker long-lasting domain access.
exampleSentence: The golden ticket gave the attacker access to every system in the domain.

definition: Making a program load a malicious library instead of the real one.
exampleSentence: DLL hijacking worked because the program searched an unsafe folder first.

definition: Using tools already on the system to avoid detection by security software.
exampleSentence: Living off the land makes attacks hard to see because only normal tools are used.

definition: Methods an attacker uses to keep access after a reboot or password change.
exampleSentence: The attacker created a hidden scheduled task for persistence on the server.

definition: An attack that changes directory queries by inserting malicious input.
exampleSentence: LDAP injection let the attacker bypass the login form of the intranet.

definition: An attack that manipulates queries to a NoSQL database through unsafe input.
exampleSentence: A NoSQL injection in the search box returned documents that users should not see.

definition: Stealing payment details by injecting malicious code into online checkout forms.
exampleSentence: Formjacking copied the card numbers that customers typed into the store checkout.
